parties:
The State ----- Appellant
Vs.
Nuru Mira ----- Accused-Respondent
full_judgment: 7. As to the nature of the injury from which Amjad died, P.Ws. 1, 2, 7 and others gave consistent evidence that accused Nuru had hurled a teta at Amjad which hit him at the ear and then pulled out the teta. P.W 3, the medical officer, found on Amjads dead body "a sharp cutting penetrating injury at the left ear, 1½ x ½ x brain cavity," and gave his opinion that the injury was caused by a sharp, pointed weapon, such as, a Shorki. This injury is the cause of death, he has said. A teta is also a pointed weapon but it has hooks. In answer to a question by the defence he said that if any hooks/hooked weapon penetrates upto the hook level and then is pulled out, then the injury might be a lacerated one. This is the evidence which the learned Judges of the High Court Division found to be materially inconsistent with the evidence of the eye witnesses that the injury was caused with a teta. If the teta penetrates upto its hook level, then a laceration may go caused if is pulled out but if it does not so penetrate, then the injury caused by it will be a straight penetrating one. The medical evidence (of P.W. 3) shows that a pointed weapon hit the ear base and penetrated upto the brain cavity. The distance between the brain cavity and the ear is not great. If a pointed weapon enters though the ear it may reached the brain cavity covering a distance of 1" or 1½". If the hook of a teta enters the body upto its full length and then is brought out the injury caused may be lacerated but if the hook does not so penetrate, there will be hardly any difference between an wound caused by a Shorki and that caused by a teta. In any way, on a single statement in the form of an opinion given by the medical officer in this case it is handle possible to come to a conclusion that the fatal injury of Amjad was caused by a shirk and not by a teta. In the substances of this case the opinion of P.W. 3 cannot be held to be materially inconsistent with the direct evidence of so many witness. Some marks of swellings were also found in the dead body of Amjad and the learned Judges observed that these were not explained by the prosecution. There is evidence that deceased Amjad was being chased along the bank of the khal by many persons including Nuru. P. W. 8 who supported the prosecution case on material particulars at the beginning, said that Amjad was assaulted by used Nure Mira with a "logi" which is a long bamboo piece. At this he was declared hostile prosecution. We think there was no necessity to declare hostile the prosecution could have simply doss examined him with Court's permission on this particular point. From this piece of evidence of P.W. 8 an attempt was made to make out a case that accused Nuru might had assaulted Amjad with a bamboo post which caused the swelling, but the fatal wound was caused by some other person. As we have found, there were only three persons who had chased Amjad upto the land of Yasin than before he was given the fatal blow. Two of these persons, namely Suhrab and Mukhtar, discontinued the chase and accused Nuns was left to hit his target. The assault took place at broad day Might and it was seen by the witnesses including the victim's father from a close distance. If any other person had caused the tata injury to his son, why they would be spared in favour of accused Nuru with whom Amjad or his father had got no grudge from before. If any body were to be falsely implicated in the case, the acquitted accused Hashern Sherif, Hanif Sharif and Kashem Sharif, who had disputed the possession of the land would have been the proper persons. They are cousins of Amjad and accused the is their relation having no claim to the land. We, therefore, find no good reason for the Informant P.W. 1 to pin point and falsely implicate Nuru Mira as the person who hurled a teta at Amjad and caused the injury therewith. It may be mentioned here that P.W. 1 has been corroborated on this point by the ejaher he had lodged within the shortest possible time. Had all these points been given due consideration by the appellate   Court, they could not have reversed the trial Court's finding. Appellate Court's finding is against the clear evidence supporting the charge that Nuru Mira had; caused the fatal injury to Amjad with a tete. Ordinarily, an order of acquittal is not interfeted with but to meet the cause of justice we find it a fit case for interference with the order of acquittal of the accused respondent We have no hesitation to hold that Nuru Mira had been rightly convicted for the murder of Amjad and that reversal of his conviction by the appellate Court is totally unjustified as its finding as to the nature of the fatal injury of Amjad is based on surmises.
